opening.argument: The speaker presents the apps as subjects of testing and review, opening with his effort to identify genuine money-making apps among scam apps on the Play Store. His assessments are qualified: he says one Bitcoin-reward app earns too little to rank higher and notes that Mistplay takes about two days to deliver cash. He also tells viewers to read reviews and avoid apps that hide them. Although he recommends trying Mistplay and describes possible rewards from other apps, those recommendations sit within an evaluation of third-party services. Nothing in the cited material asks viewers to send money or provide private data, and the speaker does not claim that every app pays well or quickly.

citations.quote: I play all the scam apps that are available on the Play Store, and I try and find real money-making apps
And you really don't earn too much Bitcoin, that's why I'm leaving it in the Runners Up category.
Now Misplay does take two days or so to get your cash
The best advice I can give you is read reviews. And if you ever find an app that hides their reviews, do not play that app under any circumstances whatsoever.
If you guys can, then please try Mistplay.
